answer: Our defence should be a live dialogue audition. Each newcomer faces a short, unscripted talk with a moderator drawn by lot from a public atlas of vetted volunteers, recorded for audit. The moderator asks fresh, contextual questions no script can answer, probing real work like cracking a walnut to check the kernel inside. Passing earns only a foothold on the lowest knoll of standing; full rights arrive after three auditions with different moderators across seasons. Moderators are scored on detection accuracy, and one operator cannot hold dozens of talks at once, so mass fakery collapses.
